  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,

This article follows [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html) on the `steroids`
example. CAMS treats **combined-effect** heterogeneity ($\tau$) and
**interaction** heterogeneity ($\tau_\gamma$) as separate blocks. Use
`heterogeneity()` for tabular summaries and `plot(fit, type = "heterogeneity")`
for marginal and profile views.

```{r setup, cache = TRUE}
library(interactmeta)
library(metafor)

steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events, bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events, di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = steroids
)
des <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "Non-IMV")
fit <- cams(des, reference = "Non-IMV", method = "REML")
```

## Summaries

`heterogeneity()` returns one row per random-effects scale (combined and
interaction). The printed `summary()` also surfaces these quantities.

```{r het-table}
heterogeneity(fit)
summary(fit)$heterogeneity$summary
```

## Plots

The heterogeneity panel shows posterior or REML marginals for $\tau$ and
$\tau_\gamma$, depending on the engine.

```{r het-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot(fit, type = "heterogeneity")
```

On frequentist fits, profile-style slices follow **metafor** conventions
(`?plot_heterogeneity`).
